The Good and Bad Of The Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act

It brings up an interesting question, though. While I deplore the use of the Commerce Clause (with the court system's consent) to expand Federal power and pass laws on matters having nothing to,do with commerce, it actually would seem appropriate for Federal law to preempt State laws to the extent it dealt with interstate travel and commerce. For instance, if I have a gun legal in Virginia and legal in Texas, I should be allowed to transport it legally through the States in between.

This is actually already the law. And it is a Federal law. But it has strict requirements i terms of how the guns have to be stored, etc. This strikes me as completely within the framework of the Constitution and rightful Federal jurisdiction. It is not so much a law on guns as on interstate travel and commerce both of which are covered (though in different provisions) in the Constitution. So, the question really is how far the Feds can step on the rights of the States in allowing otherwise prohibited things to occur in their State because it crosses borders.

I happen to think the States also have limited rights to restrict arms, but it is still an interesting question of where the line should be drawn in terms of Federal power.
